datasets.title: Geodata of Damage Assessment in Central Ramadi, Al Anbar Province, Iraq
datasets.description: This map illustrates satellite-detected damage and destruction in Ramadi City, Iraq. Using satellite imagery collected 29 January 2016 collected by the GeoEye-1 satellite, and compared with a pre-crisis Pleiades image collected 06 July 2014, UNOSAT analysis has identified 1,165 destroyed structures, 818 severely damaged structures, and 1,222 moderately damaged structures within the downtown area of Ramadi. Considerably more damage is found in surrounding areas of the city (not shown on map). Note that this analysis documents destruction occurring between 6 July 2014 and 29 January 2016, certain areas of Ramadi show destruction occurring prior to 6 July 2014. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to UNITAR / UNOSAT.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/geodata-of-damage-assessment-in-central-ramadi-al-anbar-province-iraq-january-15-2016]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts compared multi-temporal satellite imagery (Pleiades pre-crisis baseline from July 2014 and GeoEye-1 post-event from January 2016) to identify structural changes and classify buildings into three damage categories (destroyed, severely damaged, moderately damaged) through visual interpretation. The resulting geodataset contains 3,205 classified building damage records with spatial geometry and confidence assessments for downtown Ramadi.

sources.name: United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Satellite imagery analysis comparing GeoEye-1 (29 January 2016) and Pleiades (6 July 2014) imagery to detect and classify building damage in Ramadi through visual interpretation of structural destruction patterns.
